question: If the height of a vertical pole is sqrt{3} times the length of its shadow on the ground, then the angle of elevation of the sun at that time is :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let shadow length = 1 unit.

Height of pole = √3 units.

tan θ = Height ÷ Shadow = √3 ÷ 1 = √3

Since tan 60° = √3, the angle of elevation θ = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The height of the vertical pole is √3 times the length of its shadow.

 
• 
 
 θ √3x x A B C Pole Shadow

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of the shadow (BC) be x.

⇒ Height of the pole (AB) = √3x

⇒ Let the angle of elevation of the sun be θ.

⇒ In right-angled triangle ABC:

⇒ tan θ = AB ÷ BC

⇒ tan θ = √3x ÷ x

⇒ tan θ = √3

⇒ We know that tan 60° = √3

⇒ ∴ θ = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object located above the horizontal level.

Standard Trigonometric Values

tan 30° = 1 ÷ √3 | tan 45° = 1 | tan 60° = √3

Angle of Depression

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object located below the horizontal level. The angle of elevation and the angle of depression are always equal due to alternate interior angles.
